“Are you sure you don’t want to have a look? They just released the game and it’s awesome!” Timmy attempted to coax some enthusiasm into Alex, his older brother, but to no avail.

Alex had his limbs draped over the living room couch, and he seemed to have become entranced by the television screen. Timmy had just loaded up his latest Christmas present, Sims 4, into the shared computer and was extremely excited about creating his first family of Sims. Timmy entered the character design mode and the nonsensical blabbering and relaxing tunes of the game entered the ears of both Timmy and Alex, with occasional head turns by the bigger brother from the television to the computer screen..

Before long, the television had been switched off and Alex had pulled up a chair beside Timmy. Timmy, almost bursting with excitement and the amount of control he had over the Sims, chattered away about the features and the things that he could do with his creations. Alex occasionally raised a question or two about the gameplay, for he was not familiar to such simulation games. Alex himself was a First-Person-Shooter gamer and this sort of simulation game was foreign to him.

“Would you like to try a little? I’ll show you how to make them take care of the baby. “He asked, while controlled his Sims couple and their baby. Alex grunted in agreement, and then took hold of the mouse.

“Here, all you have to do is to click this and that, followed by this option at the top, and she’s being fed!” Timmy could hardly control his enjoyment of the game, for simply watching the Sims execute his commands made the 9-year-old display a toothless grin. “Cool, this is really awesome! Let me play for a little longer.” Alex replied, his eyes locked onto the computer screen. Timmy’s grin faded a little, before smiling again. He gave in to his older brother’s request, for it was just a little bit longer of waiting, that’s all. “Try to make the baby play with the teddy bear! C’mon, make it!” Timmy cajoled Alex to do as his said, but to no avail. The baby went out into the garden instead and thereafter, fell asleep on the grass. Alex giggled as a pop-up window appeared, informing the brothers that another instance of the baby being left unattended would result in social services taking the baby away.

“No! What are you doing?” Timmy exclaimed. Any prior happiness had clearly vanished from his face. “Stop it!”

Timmy tried to wrestle control of the mouse back from his 15-year-old brother, but it was a futile attempt. Alex was part of the wrestling team and it was clear that a 70 pound pre-pubescent boy wouldn’t move a 170 pound hunk of human muscle. Alex swatted away Timmy’s hands and shoved him back, sending Timmy flying off his chair onto the ground below.

A tear or two rolled from Timmy’s eyes, but he knew that crying wouldn’t help. Their parents were out working and it wasn’t right for a man to cry, anyway. That’s what Alex always told him. Timmy nursed his bruised elbow and sat next to Alex, watching helplessly from the sidelines.

Alex continued exerting his control on the family, his actions tinged with a taste of sadism. The baby had grown up into a pretty young girl, but she was failing her studies because she wasn’t doing any of her homework. To make matters worse, and to Timmy’s horror, Alex had killed off one of the parents by removing one of the doors of a room. Timmy watched from behind, crying out against Alex’s every action, but his protests fell upon deaf ears. Before long, right after a fire engulfed the family home, social services came and took the young girl away.

Satisfied, Alex stood up and resumed his position on the couch, leaving Timmy with a destroyed family.

Our bodies have a consciousness of our own. From a point even beyond our birth, we begin to unconsciously suppress this 'other' consciousness, and assume control.

At least, that's how it was supposed to be. It was what the latest medical journals had told us, and what was already written into the texts of all the prestigious universities across the country. This man, however, was a different case.

I had read his medical profile beforehand, so I was surprised from my patient when a rather fragile yet good-looking man stepped into my office. He sat down in a chair, the collar of the wooly green overcoat he wore brushing against the jaw-length brown hair that he sported.

This was not a regular office, but then again, I was not a regular doctor. I gestured for him to begin speaking, and withdrew a pen from my breast pocket. I tapped on the clipboard as he began to gather his words.

"It... it happens sometimes. I can feeling it coming almost, like the feeling when you're about to faint. It comes slowly, but it comes, and I can feel an intense hatred for everyone around me, but I know that this hatred is not my own." The man shuffled in his seat, a metallic sound coming from the chains of the handcuffs he wore.

Strange, I thought to myself. Never have I placed handcuffs on any of my patients. I jotted it down, noting to myself that it seemed he had placed them on himself – some sort of restraint. Looking back at the information that had been gathered beforehand, it seemed that he used to be a medical practitioner of some sort as well, but had since lost his job in disrepute. The handsome yet dishevelled man who sat before me seemed to verify the information. I paused as he began to speak again.

"No matter how hard I try, it seems to overtake me eventually, and... and when I awake, I am always somewhere strange. But this not the cause of my concerns." He paused, seemingly gathering himself. "Every time this has happened – it is the third now – I always awake, and there are people who have been killed around me. There is no way for me to tell if it was I that did this, but it seems to be so. The last time that this happened, I turned myself in to the police."

I nodded. So far, all the information had been in line with the folder that I held in my hands. This man killed at random without his knowing, and it seemed that the other consciousness that takes over had slaughtered these victims in the most gruesome ways possible.

"I stayed the night in the compound, but when I awoke, I was at the door of the police station yet again, but this time all the overnight officers were dead. I... I just don't know what to do anymore. I hate myself for doing this, but I don't know how to make it stop. Please, doctor, I am a peaceful man. Surely there is something you can do."

For the first time since he had entered through the door, I spoke. "Please remain here. I shall return shortly." I stepped outside, careful to lock the door behind me with the patient handcuffed inside. In my profession, these kinds of precautions could not be overlooked.

"Henrietta," I began. "I am ready to prepare the treatment for the patient. Please gather the medical records for Dr. Henry Jekyll."

"The vigorous man industriously striving for the improvement of his condition acts neither more nor less than the lethargic man who sluggishly takes things as they come. For to do nothing and to be idle are also action, they too determine the course of events. Wherever the conditions for human interference are present, man acts no matter whether he interferes or refrains from interfering. He who endures what he could change acts no less than he who interferes in order to attain another result. A man who abstains from influencing the operation of physiological and instinctive factors which he could influence also acts. Action is not only doing but no less omitting to do what possibly could be done.

We may say that action is the manifestation of a man's will. But this would not add anything to our knowledge. For the term will means nothing else than man's faculty to choose between different states of affairs, to prefer one, to set aside the other, and to behave according to the decision made in aiming at the chosen state and forsaking the other."

-- Mises "Human Action"
